one-variable.t: With a **single weight**, the loss is a curve: the weight runs along the bottom and the loss is the height. This is the picture from the earlier checkpoints.

two-variables.h: TWO WEIGHTS: A FLOOR OF CHOICES
two-variables.t: With two weights, every choice of **(w₁, w₂)** is a point on a flat floor. **Two numbers** are needed to say where you are standing.

surface.h: THE LOSS LIFTS INTO A SURFACE
surface.t: At each point of the floor, raise the loss as a **height**. The flat floor becomes a **surface**, here a bowl with its lowest point above **(3, 1)**.

point-on-surface.t: Each position of the model is a point on the surface: the floor point **(1, 3)** holds the weights, and the height above it is the **loss, 12**.

many-variables.t: Real models have **thousands or millions** of weights. We cannot draw that landscape, but **nothing in the rules changes**.

parameter-vector.h: A WEIGHT VECTOR AND ITS GRADIENT
parameter-vector.t: The weights form a **vector w**. The gradient has **one entry per weight**: one partial derivative for each. Same count, same order.

ml-loss.t: A tiny model with 3 weights: the weights make a prediction, the prediction gives **one loss number**, and from it we get **one slope for each weight**.
